content:
The test image shows soybean field rows with widespread yellowing and browning of whole plants — wilting, dying leaves, row-pattern damage, while background plants remain green. Key features: interveinal-looking chlorosis/necrosis, whole-plant decline, some rows severely affected.

Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome, Phytophthora, Brown_Stem_Rot. Let me compare reference images.

Comparing the three reference images to the test image:

- **Phytophthora** (train_003): Shows wilted/dead soybean plants with brown attached leaves next to healthy green plants — **very similar** to the test image's field-level pattern
- **SDS** (train_003): Shows close-up of a badly decomposed stem with blue fungal growth — different from what the test shows
- **Brown_Stem_Rot** (train_003): Shows interveinal chlorosis on individual leaves — not the whole-plant field-level collapse seen in test image

The test image clearly shows rows of soybean plants with whole-plant wilting and death, leaves still attached and brown, while background plants remain green. This matches the Phytophthora description: "general yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward, followed by wilting and death... leaves typically stay attached after plant death" — and the Phytophthora reference image shows essentially the same field-level scene.
